title: Shadow judging on a gate runner: a copy of each judged verdict is judged on the runner on the same immutable inputs, recorded beside the primary's, never deciding or delaying a landing; a disagreement reaches the supervisor once, and verdicts on unequal inputs are never compared
prompt:
Prerequisite: objective 035 (every `task.gated` binds `class`, `inputs` {base, candidate, controller, scenarios_sha256, scenario} and `env` {host, toolchain, runner}); assign this one after 035 has landed, and build on its `inputs` and `env`, never on a second reading of your own. Also needs the gate runner's dispatcher as it is in the controller tree after the runner-env change (deploy/gate-runner.sh with deploy/gate-runner/{remote.sh,setup.sh}, branch runner-env ce29c546): in production the integrator runs the controller's deploy/gate-runner.sh (outside any sandbox); rsi/scenarios/036.sh, which runs inside the gate's sandbox where the controller's deploy/ is not visible, copies it from the tree under judgement (its working directory: deploy/ is protected, so it is the base's) and installs a fake runner with its setup.sh; a tree without it cannot shadow and is unsolved, exit 1.

Read deploy/gate-runner.sh and deploy/gate-runner/README.md (you may not edit them): its arguments `<runner> <source.git> <base> <candidate> <scenarios> <out>`, its environment (GATE_RUNNER_SSH, GATE_RUNNER_REMOTE_BIN, GATE_RUNNER_REGISTRY, GATE_RUNNER_RETRIES, GATE_RUNNER_MIN_FREE_MEMORY_MB, the stage timeouts), its exit statuses and what it writes: `<out>/<job>/{verdict.json,gate.log,record.json}` (record.json's `result`: `verdict`, `transport`, `timeout`, `result`), nothing when it refuses (exit 3). In crates/spawn-cli/src/integrate.rs: `record()`, the judging's `gated` closure and its `task.gated` record (with 035's `inputs` and `env`), how a gate thread starts and ends, and the base warm (crates/spawn-cli/src/integrate/warm.rs: never on a landing's path, one at a time, `setpriv --pdeathsig TERM` from a thread that lives as long as the child, its own process group, the pid file and `take_over`): a shadow follows that pattern. In crates/spawn-cli/src/dispatch.rs and dispatch/digest.rs: `Why`, `is_news`, `read_plan`'s host items, and how an item is told once (the tag `host <id>` a delivered digest files, read back by the store's queries, e.g. GATE_BASE_DISAGREES_ALERTS in crates/spawn-postgres/src/missions.rs). crates/spawn-postgres/sql/schema.sql: `spawn_integrator_record` (the record types it allows, the task state check) and `spawn_control_apply`.

The problem. Gates are the fleet's bottleneck: in the 48 h to 2026-11-09 12:00, 112 gates, mean 17 min, max 101; a reported task waited about 5 h for its gate. A second host can judge (deploy/gate-runner.sh ships a gate run to a runner and brings its verdict back; a real dispatch to spawn-runner judged 984d0592 -> 45c61205 accepted in 1258 s), but before a runner's verdict may decide anything (milestone M3) it must be shown to agree with the primary's. The owner's rule for this milestone (M2, 2026-11-09): the primary and the runner evaluate exactly the same immutable inputs, and shadow results never influence landing. Two verdicts on different inputs are not a comparison.

Required behaviour (the contract the gate checks).
1. With SPAWN_GATE_SHADOW_RUNNER set (the runner's name for the transport; unset or empty: no shadow, the runner is never called) and `deploy/gate-runner.sh` present in the controller of the mission's gate directory (the directory two levels above it), after the primary records an `accepted` or `rejected` verdict that a gate run gave (035's `env` is not null), the integrator runs `<controller>/deploy/gate-runner.sh <runner> <the gate's repository: its first argument> <inputs.base> <inputs.candidate> <the gate directory> <a private out directory>` in the background, in the integrator's own environment (the GATE_RUNNER_* variables are read there). At most one shadow runs at a time; a verdict while one runs is not shadowed (skipped, never queued); SPAWN_GATE_SHADOW_EVERY=N (a whole number, default 1) shadows every N-th such verdict.
2. A landing never waits for a shadow, and a shadow never changes a task's state, a landing, a halt, gate_rejections, gate_aborts or any budget: the record is beside the verdict, not part of it.
3. Its end is recorded once, `task.shadow_gated` {`id`, `revision` (the primary's), `base`, `candidate` (the primary's `inputs`), `runner`, `result` (record.json's `result`, or `refused` when the dispatcher wrote none and exited 3), `verdict` (verdict.json's `accepted` or `rejected`, else null), `exit` (the dispatcher's status), `seconds`, `inputs` (035's object for what the runner was given and received: `base`, `candidate`, `controller` (`.controller` of the controller, read when the shadow starts), `scenarios_sha256` (035's digest of the scenario set the runner received: if the gate directory may change between your reading and the dispatcher's copy, ship a snapshot you read), `scenario`: null, the dispatcher ships no task scenario), `env` {`host`: null (the dispatcher does not report the runner's host name), `toolchain`: the text after `| base cache: toolchain ` on the first such line of the runner's gate.log, or null, `runner`}, `primary` (the primary's verdict), `primary_env` (the primary's `env`), `unequal` (the names of the `inputs` fields, among base, candidate, controller, scenarios_sha256 and scenario, whose values differ from the primary's `inputs`, in any order; [] when none), `agrees` (true or false only when `unequal` is empty and both sides are verdicts; null otherwise: never a comparison of verdicts on unequal inputs)}. The record changes no table (the fold ignores it).
4. A `task.shadow_gated` with `agrees` false is told to the supervisor once: a digest item of its own (news, not a condition) naming the task (`#<id>`), the word shadow, the runner, both verdicts and both environments. An agreement and a record with `agrees` null are told nothing.
5. A stopping integrator TERMs its shadow as it does its warm (nothing it starts outlives it unaccounted); the shadow's out directory is removed when its record is written.

The gate judges this with rsi/scenarios/036.sh. A real loop runs one resident, `shadow`, of one gated mission on a fake engine; the primary's gate (SPAWN_GATE) and the runner's (the controller tree's scripts/rsi/gate.sh, which the dispatcher ships) are recording fakes, each noting its arguments, the runner's also the digest of the scenario set it received; the runner is a root under $HOME installed by the controller's deploy/gate-runner/setup.sh and an `ssh` stub. (0) task A with the integrator started without SPAWN_GATE_SHADOW_RUNNER: accepted and landed, no `task.shadow_gated` and no call to the runner. Then one integrator with SPAWN_GATE_SHADOW_RUNNER=bb-runner: (1) task B, accepted on both; the runner's gate holds until released: B's shadow reaches the runner within 60 s of its verdict, B lands while the runner's gate is held and before any shadow record; released, the record names what the runner's gate was given and received, `unequal` [], `agrees` true, the runner's toolchain, the primary's env. (2) task C, accepted on the primary and rejected on the runner: C lands, gate_rejections unchanged, `agrees` false, and within 60 s a digest to the supervisor names #C, the runner and `shadow`. (3) task D: the primary's gate adds a file to the gate directory while it runs, so the runner receives another set: `inputs` is what the runner received; when its scenarios_sha256 is not the primary's, `unequal` names it and `agrees` is null. (4) 20 s later the supervisor was told of C's disagreement once and of B's and D's never. On the live main (984d059) it fails at (1) in about 90 s: "(1) no shadow of task #2's verdict reached the runner within 60 s"; on objective 035's reference implementation alone the same. A reference implementation (not to land) passed it five times in 77-82 s; mutants of it fail: one whose integrator waits for the shadow before the landing (at (1)), one that computes `agrees` on unequal inputs (at (3)), one whose digest item is not told once (at (4)).

What it saves. Nothing by itself: it is the measurement that lets milestone M3 send gates to runners with evidence that they judge as the primary does (M2's exit: 20 or more shadows, every disagreement explained, the runner's wall clock within 1.3x the primary's).

Rules: never edit the protected paths, which the gate rejects: rsi/, scripts/ (scripts/rsi/, scripts/blackbox/, scripts/e2e.sh among them), deploy/, all of web/ except web/src/ and web/index.html, rust-toolchain files and .cargo/. The gate also rejects fewer runnable tests than the base (do not delete, rename, ignore or disable tests), any lint relaxation and any build-time code. The gate builds offline from the cargo caches already on the host: a new crate builds only if it is already in ~/.cargo/registry. Keep every existing check green (clippy -D warnings, the workspace tests, the e2e, the black-box scenarios, the web build) and add tests of your own for the new behaviour.
